headline: Sales grow on oncology; acquisition charge drives a loss

kpis.label: EBITDA
kpis.delta: swung to profit from a loss

summary_short: Merck posted $16.6B in Q2 2026 sales, up 5.1% y/y, but a $2.31 per-share charge for the Terns acquisition swung GAAP EPS to a $0.54 loss from $1.76 a year ago.
summary_long: Q2 2026 sales rose 5.1% y/y (4% ex-FX) to $16.6B, led by KEYTRUDA/KEYTRUDA QLEX (+5% to $8.4B) and WINREVAIR (+75% to $588M); Animal Health grew 8%. GAAP EPS swung to a $0.54 loss from $1.76 a year ago, driven mainly by a $2.31/share charge for the Terns acquisition. Gross margin fell to 73.5% from 77.5% on higher intangible amortization and inventory write-downs; R&D nearly doubled to $9.7B on the Terns charge and higher clinical spend. Cash rose to $6.8B q/q while long-term debt climbed to $51.1B. Merck raised FY2026 sales guidance to $66.3-67.3B but cut non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.66-2.76 (from $5.04-5.16) on new Terns and Cidara charges.

Ledger notes: (1) GAAP and non-GAAP EPS both include a $2.31/share one-time charge for the Terns Pharmaceuticals acquisition (a $6.8B all-cash deal that closed this quarter); non-GAAP EPS excludes acquisition/divestiture and restructuring costs plus equity-security gains/losses, so the two EPS figures diverge sharply (-$0.54 GAAP vs -$0.13 non-GAAP) by design, not error. (2) The effective tax rate was -95.9% on a pretax loss of $683M because the Terns charge carried no associated tax benefit -- an unusual rate reconciled directly from the release's own table, not a data error. (3) FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $2.66-$2.76 is a large step down from the prior $5.04-$5.16 range, but per the release this reflects newly added one-time charges for the Terns and Cidara Therapeutics acquisitions ($2.31 and $3.62 per share respectively), not a change in underlying operating outlook. (4) Long-term debt rose to $51.1B (+50.4% y/y); the release does not itself attribute this to acquisition financing, so that link is inference, not company-disclosed fact, and is omitted from drivers[].

drivers.explanation: CEO Robert Davis cited strong execution and growing contributions from new launches, highlighting the LIPFENDRA FDA approval and regulatory/clinical progress across oncology, HIV and immunology.

Growth driven by oncology strength (KEYTRUDA/KEYTRUDA QLEX, WELIREG) plus cardiometabolic and respiratory launches (WINREVAIR), partially offset by declining diabetes-franchise sales (JANUVIA/JANUMET).
Gross margin fell to 73.5% from 77.5% y/y on higher amortization of intangible assets and inventory write-downs, even as gross profit dollars were roughly flat.
GAAP EPS swung to a loss mainly on a $2.31/share charge for the Terns acquisition, versus a $0.07/share Hengrui Pharma license charge a year earlier.
Net loss reflects a $5.7B one-time R&D charge for the Terns acquisition and higher clinical spending, partly offset by a $200M R&D reduction from the Blackstone funding deal.
